cmd.up.long:
Start all services and dependencies for the current project.

Raioz auto-detects the config file (raioz.yaml, .raioz.json) and
the runtime of each service (Docker Compose, Dockerfile, npm, Go, Make, etc.).

Services start in dependency order. Infrastructure (images) starts first,
then application services with their native tools.
cmd.down.long:
Bring down all services and infrastructure for the current project.

Use --all to stop all workspace services and infrastructure.
Use --prune-shared to also stop shared infrastructure if no other active projects use it.
cmd.status.long:
Show detailed status information for all services including:
- Status (running/stopped)
- Health status (healthy/unhealthy/starting)
- Uptime
- Resource usage (CPU, Memory)
- Version/commit information
- Last update time
cmd.logs.long:
View logs for one or more services.

If no service is specified and --all is not set, shows logs for all services.
Use --all to explicitly show logs for all services.
Use --follow to follow logs in real-time.
Use --tail N to show only the last N lines.
cmd.clean.short: Clean up stopped services and unused resources
cmd.clean.long:
Clean up stopped services and unused Docker resources.

By default, cleans stopped services for the current project.
Use flags to clean additional resources or all projects.
cmd.check.long:
Validate the configuration without starting anything.

Checks:
- raioz.yaml parses and every field is known
- each service has a runtime raioz can detect
- dependsOn references exist
- proxy requirements (mkcert, certificates)
- host ports: explicit clashes and ports already taken

A meta config (kind: meta) is checked project by project.

check does not look at what is running: use 'raioz status' or 'raioz health' for that.

Exit codes:
- 0: the configuration is valid
- 1: at least one issue was found
cmd.ci.short: Validate the project and pull its images, with JSON output
cmd.ci.long:
Validate raioz.yaml and pull the dependency images, for CI pipelines.

Runs the preflight checks, loads and validates the config, and pulls the
images (skip with --skip-pull, or stop after validation with --only-validate).
The result is a JSON report on stdout; the exit code is 1 when something fails.

ci does not start services or dependencies. To bring the project up in a
pipeline use 'raioz up' and 'raioz down'.
cmd.compare.long:
Compare your local .raioz.json with a production Docker Compose file
to identify differences in images, ports, volumes, and dependencies.

This helps ensure that your local development environment matches production
as closely as possible.
cmd.health.short: Check project health and manage local project lifecycle
cmd.health.long:
Check if the project is running and report its health status.

Uses the health endpoint defined in raioz.yaml (e.g., health: /api/health)
or falls back to checking if containers and processes are alive.
cmd.ignore.long:
Manage services that should be ignored during dependency resolution.

Ignored services will not be cloned, built, or started. However, if other
services depend on ignored services, a warning will be shown.

Example:
  raioz ignore add service-name
  raioz ignore remove service-name
  raioz ignore list
cmd.ignore.add.short: Add a service to the ignore list
cmd.ignore.add.long:
Add a service to the ignore list. The service will not be cloned,
built, or started during raioz up.

Example:
  raioz ignore add old-service
cmd.ignore.remove.short: Remove a service from the ignore list
cmd.ignore.remove.long:
Remove a service from the ignore list. The service will be processed
normally on the next raioz up.

Example:
  raioz ignore remove service-name
cmd.ignore.list.long:
List all services that are currently in the ignore list.

Example:
  raioz ignore list
cmd.init.short: Initialize a new raioz.yaml configuration file
cmd.init.long:
Scan the current directory and generate a raioz.yaml configuration file.

Detects services from subdirectory structure and infers infrastructure
dependencies from .env files (DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, etc.).
cmd.list.long:
List all active projects tracked in the global state.

This command shows:
- Project names
- Last execution time
- Number of active services per project
- Workspace paths

Filters:
- Use --filter to show only projects matching a name pattern
- Use --status to filter by service status (running, stopped)
cmd.migrate.short: Convert a Docker Compose file to raioz.yaml
cmd.migrate.long:
Convert a Docker Compose file to raioz.yaml.

Services with `build:` become raioz services (local code); services that only
name an image become dependencies. What cannot be carried over is listed so
you can finish it by hand.
cmd.ports.short: List all ports in use by active projects
cmd.version.long:
Show version information for raioz including:
- Binary version
- Git commit (if available)
- Build date
- Supported schema version
cmd.volumes.long:
Manage Docker volumes associated with a project.

Subcommands:
  list    List all volumes for the project
  remove  Remove specific or all project volumes

Examples:
  raioz volumes list
  raioz volumes remove --all
  raioz volumes remove my-project_postgres-data
cmd.volumes.list.long:
List all Docker volumes associated with the project.

Shows volume names, their source (service or infra), and whether
they are shared with other projects.

Examples:
  raioz volumes list
  raioz volumes list --project myproject
cmd.volumes.remove.long:
Remove Docker volumes associated with the project.

You can remove specific volumes by name or all volumes with --all.
Volumes shared with other projects are excluded unless forced.

Examples:
  raioz volumes remove --all
  raioz volumes remove --all --force
  raioz volumes remove my-project_postgres-data

cmd.restart.long:
Restart one or more services for the current project.

Specify service names to restart specific services.
Use --all to restart all services (excluding infra by default).
Use --include-infra with --all to also restart infrastructure.
Use --force-recreate to tear down and recreate containers.

error.proxy_mkcert_missing_suggestion:

  Alternatively set `proxy.tls: letsencrypt` for a real public domain, or remove `proxy:` from raioz.yaml to skip HTTPS entirely.
error.proxy_dir_corrupted: proxy state directory %s is not writable or has been replaced by a directory at the Caddyfile path. This is the issue 015 trap: a Caddy container with --restart unless-stopped came back after the dir was wiped (tmpfs reboot, manual cleanup) and Docker re-created the bind-mount source as root-owned. From that point every `raioz up` fails until the tree is removed.
error.proxy_dir_corrupted_suggestion:
Remove the corrupt tree and re-run `raioz up`:
    sudo rm -rf %s
  Recent raioz versions store proxy state under ~/.local/state/raioz/ instead of /tmp to prevent recurrence; legacy /tmp paths are cleaned automatically on the next successful `raioz down`.

Verify that all required tools and configurations are in place.

Checks:
- Docker daemon is installed and running
- Docker Compose v2 is available
- Git is installed
- Disk space is sufficient
- Raioz configuration directory exists

Examples:
  raioz doctor

cmd.hosts.short: Print the /etc/hosts line for this project's proxy
cmd.switch.short: Free colliding host ports and bring up the cwd project
cmd.env.short: Show environment variables for a service
cmd.env.long:
Display all environment variables that a service would receive,
including variables from .env files and auto-injected service discovery variables.

cmd.clone.short: Clone a repo and start the project

clone.no_config: No raioz.yaml found. Run raioz init to generate one.
cmd.dashboard.long:
Opens an interactive terminal dashboard showing all services,
their status, logs, and resource usage in real-time.
Alias: raioz tui

error.secret_in_yaml: raioz.yaml contains what looks like a %s (line ~%d). Secrets must never live in the yaml.
error.secret_in_yaml_suggestion: Move the credential to environment variables, a .env file, or a secret manager. For git auth see ADR-036 (yaml hygiene policy).
error.path_escapes_repo: path %q resolves outside the project directory (would resolve to %s)
error.path_escapes_repo_suggestion: Paths in raioz.yaml must resolve inside the project directory. Use relative paths like ./api/ or ./scripts/setup.sh. For a multi-repo workspace where services live in sibling repos, declare workspaceRoot: (e.g. ..) to widen the containment boundary.
error.path_in_system_dir: path %q targets system directory %s, which raioz refuses to touch
error.path_in_system_dir_suggestion: Move the file inside the project, or use a different mechanism (env var, host volume mount).

warning.image_latest: dependency %q uses image %q with :latest; pin a specific tag for reproducibility
warning.volume_system_dir: dependency %q mounts the system directory %s into its container; the image gets whatever it holds — mount a narrower path if you can

launcher.drain_timeout: Service '%s': launcher build did not produce container '%s' within %v — running stop: anyway. Check `docker ps -a` if an orphan appears.

down.selective_sibling_owned: %s: sibling-owned (project: %s) — leaving it up. Run `cd %s && raioz down` to stop it from its own project.

cmd.yaml.lint.short: Report the raioz version each used field requires
cmd.yaml.lint.long: Walks the raioz.yaml in the current directory (or --file) and reports, for each populated field, the raioz version that introduced it. An unknown field fails the lint.
down.selective_deferred: %s: deferred to sibling at up time — nothing to tear down here
down.selective_shared_kept: %s: shared with sibling projects, leaving it up
compare.no_differences: No differences found. Local configuration matches production.
lint.version_none: declared version: (none) — add `version: %q` to your raioz.yaml to lock the schema
warning.version_missing: no 'version:' field declared in raioz.yaml; add `version: "%s"` to lock the schema your config targets — see docs/CONFIG_REFERENCE.md#versioning
warning.version_malformed: raioz.yaml declares version: %q which is not a recognized schema number (expected an integer like %q). This binary will load the config as if version: %q — see docs/CONFIG_REFERENCE.md#versioning
warning.version_newer: raioz.yaml declares version: %q but this binary supports version: %q. Fields introduced in newer schema versions will be ignored. Update raioz to a newer release.
warning.version_older: raioz.yaml declares version: %q but this binary expects version: %q. Field semantics may have changed across the bump. Run `raioz migrate yaml` to update the file.
warning.unknown_field: %s: %s — field ignored. Check for typos or fields from a newer raioz version.
warning.legacy_ports: dependency '%s' uses legacy `ports:`; consider migrating to `publish:` (host-side opt-in) and `expose:` (container-side declaration) for clearer semantics

  Add one of these to %s, or check that the path exists and is accessible.
error.service_start_hint.default: Check the service logs for details. Try starting the service manually.
error.service_start_hint.compose: Check the service's docker-compose.yml for errors. Try running 'docker compose up' directly in the service directory.
error.service_start_hint.dockerfile: The build or the run step failed. Try 'docker build .' in the service directory, then check for a bound port, a missing env file, or an unreachable network.
error.service_start_hint.npm: Check package.json scripts. Try running 'npm run dev' directly in the service directory.
error.service_start_hint.go: Check for compilation errors. Try running 'go run .' directly in the service directory.
error.service_start_hint.make: Check the Makefile targets. Try running 'make dev' directly in the service directory.
error.service_start_hint.command: Run the service's 'command:' from raioz.yaml directly in its directory and read what it prints.
error.service_start_hint.python: Check for missing dependencies. Try running the start command directly in the service directory.
error.service_start_hint.rust: Check for compilation errors. Try running 'cargo run' directly in the service directory.
error.service_start_hint.image: Check that the Docker image exists and can be pulled. Try 'docker pull <image>' manually.
error.dependency_start_hint_compose:
Check the compose file for hardcoded subnets or ports.
  Verify referenced env files exist and are readable.
  Check for port conflicts: raioz ports
error.dependency_start_hint_image:
Check that Docker is running: docker info
  Check that the image exists: docker pull %s
  Check for port conflicts: raioz ports
error.pre_hook_failed_suggestion:
The 'pre' command in raioz.yaml failed. This usually means:
  - You're not logged in to your secrets manager (try the login command first)
  - The script doesn't exist or isn't executable (check permissions)
  - A required tool is missing (check the command works manually)
error.pre_up_hook_failed_suggestion:
The 'preUp' command in raioz.yaml runs AFTER infra/sibling spawn but BEFORE service start. Common causes:
  - The dep your hook talks to is not reachable from the host (use the published host:port, or run the bootstrap inside a container)
  - The dep didn't actually come up — check 'raioz status'
  - The command works locally but is missing env vars — re-export them in the hook
